lead.headline: Mexico captures cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' as 11 die in Sinaloa fighting
lead.dek: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list; four soldiers and seven alleged gunmen were killed in Guasave
body: Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, the cartel leader known as "El Chapo Isidro" and one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, in an overnight operation in Guasave, Sinaloa, that left at least 11 people dead, Mexico's Defense Ministry said Saturday.

Seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed, the ministry said. The firefight began about 7 p.m. Friday and spread across the city, with gunmen burning vehicles at roadblocks and helicopters firing overhead, The Associated Press reported; troops did not extract Meza Flores until about 4 a.m. Saturday. He was flown to Mexico City with two lieutenants, and five other suspects were detained.

Meza Flores led the Beltran Leyva cartel before founding his own group, an ally of the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Mayos" faction, and the United States had offered a $5 million reward for his arrest. Mexico said U.S. intelligence helped the operation. Security Secretary Omar Garcia Harfuch said troops would stay in Sinaloa, calling the arrests "an important step in pacifying Sinaloa."

briefs.headline: Trump says he will work with Democrats on 10% card rate cap
briefs.summary: "I would do it," he told Fox News Saturday of a 10% cap; the median card rate is about 22.2%, the New York Fed found. Banks fought the idea when he raised it in January.

briefs.headline: Trump orders contractors to clear Congress replies with White House
briefs.summary: The order issued late Friday tells federal contractors to consult the administration on congressional inquiries and withhold what it deems privileged, or risk their contracts.

briefs.headline: ICE arrests 2 on Seattle jet bridge; Alaska Airlines objects
briefs.summary: Officers detained two Mexican nationals boarding a Los Angeles flight Saturday; DHS said both overstayed visas and one threw coffee at agents. Gov. Bob Ferguson said ICE is "out of control."

briefs.headline: FBI investigates apparent hack of national crime database
briefs.summary: A person familiar with the matter told AP Saturday the NCIC, which holds fugitive and criminal-history records, was breached; CNN first reported it. The FBI declined to comment.

briefs.headline: Bahrain says Iranian attack set fire to industrial facility
briefs.summary: The Interior Ministry reported material damage and no injuries late Saturday; the IRGC said it struck U.S. positions at two Bahraini bases and two Patriot radars. The U.S. had not commented.

briefs.headline: Fire at Indonesian candy factory kills 3; 36 unaccounted for
briefs.summary: The blaze began Saturday afternoon at the Fonusa Agung Mulia plant in Banten province west of Jakarta and was still burning Sunday, rescue official Rizky Dwianto said. The cause is under investigation.

briefs.headline: Russian drone hits apartment block near Kyiv; 14 unaccounted for
briefs.summary: A section of the five-story building in Dymer was destroyed overnight Sunday, regional chief Tymur Tkachenko said; a woman and a child were injured. Zelensky said 14 may be under the rubble.

briefs.headline: COP31 presidency floats draft that again omits fossil fuels
briefs.summary: The text released Sunday in Antalya, Turkey, cites only the earlier pledge to transition away from oil, gas and coal and concedes warming will pass 1.5 C; President Murat Kurum said delegates reconvene Sunday to approve it.

briefs.headline: State now says 40,000 could lose Medicaid under work rules
briefs.summary: The Department of Human Services raised its estimate from 33,000 after federal rules narrowed the health exemption, the WV Center on Budget and Policy said; about 160,000 expansion enrollees face the January rule.

briefs.headline: Auditor's office left schools' money questions unanswered
briefs.summary: The Education Department said Nov. 16 it had no reply to a July 9 letter asking Hunt's office to account for tax-sale surplus owed to a school fund; the office said Wednesday it had sent $506,875.

briefs.headline: Poll puts Justice ahead of Morrisey in 2028 GOP primary test
briefs.summary: A WMOV/American Pulse survey of 708 voters Nov. 12-18 had Justice at 43% to Morrisey's 28.4% among Republicans; Morrisey's favorability was 35.8% to 52.8% unfavorable.

briefs.headline: National Guard lays wreath for Spc. Beckstrom in Grafton
briefs.summary: Guard members held the ceremony Friday at the West Virginia National Cemetery, nearly a year after the 20-year-old died on Thanksgiving Day of wounds from a Washington ambush shooting.

regional.item: Huntington's new Green List names six landlords and a dozen rentals that passed voluntary inspections; WSAZ found one boarded up.
The Parkersburg Utility Board closes Avery Street between 8th and 9th streets from 8 a.m. Monday for water line work.
Fenwick pastor Christopher Teets, 35, pleaded not guilty to two felony child sexual abuse image charges, Lootpress reported Saturday.
The eastbound Exit 139 ramp at Sandstone is open again after bridge rehabilitation closed it from April 1, Summers County 911 confirmed.

away.item: The McCullough Free Library hosts a free Smithsonian talk on the Grateful Dead's influences Dec. 1 at 6:30 p.m., its fourth of 12.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Community Fund gave out nearly $8,000 in fall grants Nov. 11 after 19 nonprofits applied; not every request was funded in full.
Four Topsail High band members march in Thursday's 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, which steps off at 8:30 a.m. on NBC and Peacock.

briefs.headline: CNC urban bear study gets $348,715 in federal funding
briefs.summary: Vanessa Fetterly and Laura Graham have analyzed more than 100 droppings residents found since spring 2025 to learn what draws bears into the city; trail cameras on city land were added this year.

briefs.headline: Quesnel mother seeks tougher sentences for traffickers
briefs.summary: A year after Kennedy Grace Crowe, 26, died of a fentanyl overdose, Tara Marshall's 57 Days campaign has Mayor Coralee Oakes' backing; MP Todd Doherty plans a private member's bill.

briefs.headline: Death outside Port Hardy hospital follows 5 p.m. ER closure
briefs.summary: Paramedics found a patient in the parking lot at 5:11 p.m. Thursday, minutes after the daily closing; Island Health is reviewing. The ER has shut at 5 p.m. since 2023, with patients sent 45 km to Port McNeill.

briefs.headline: Kelowna kept nearly 12% staff raise quiet until after election
briefs.summary: The city's negotiator said the Oct. 19 CUPE deal was kept from the media by agreement with the union and called the criticism fair; the Canadian Taxpayers Federation said a news release was the bare minimum.

briefs.headline: Bains wins Ontario Liberal leadership on third ballot
briefs.summary: The former federal industry minister took 50.3% Saturday in Toronto, ahead of MPP Lee Fairclough; he has no seat at Queen's Park and is the third leader since Kathleen Wynne quit in 2018.

briefs.headline: U.S. senator confirms Hegseth memo limiting Canada ties
briefs.summary: Sen. Mike Rounds said in Halifax Saturday the directive, first reported by the Washington Post, limits flag officer meetings and think-tank events but not NORAD, NATO or Five Eyes; McGuinty said he has seen no change.

briefs.headline: BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit after eight-year flight
briefs.summary: ESA announced Saturday that its MPO module, with Japan's Mio still attached, was captured into orbit after a burn set for 1:24 p.m. EST, Nature reported. It is the second craft to orbit Mercury. The pair separate Dec. 9.

briefs.headline: Wolbachia mosquitoes cut arbovirus infections 69% in Brazil
briefs.summary: A trial of 5,757 children in 58 Belo Horizonte school clusters cut dengue and chikungunya infections 68.6%, Emory-led researchers told the tropical medicine society meeting Saturday. The results are not yet peer reviewed.

briefs.headline: Inner ear study challenges Nobel-winning map of hearing
briefs.summary: OHSU-led researchers reported Friday in Science Advances that low-frequency sound vibrates distant points of the guinea pig cochlea almost at once, not one spot per pitch, a finding they say bears on cochlear implant design.

briefs.headline: SpaceX Dragon returns station research to the Pacific
briefs.summary: The CRS-35 capsule splashed down off California at 5:03 p.m. EST Saturday, 29 hours after undocking, with samples including a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel used to study vascular aging. It launched Oct. 13.

briefs.headline: Stanford posts rival human-written Riemann proof draft
briefs.summary: Ravi Vakil posted Alessandro Masullo's draft Friday, calling it "all human, with no AI," and flagged gaps eight hours later; Anthropic's Levent Alpoge has released his Claude proof only as Lean code in 14 packages.

briefs.headline: UN talks end with no binding rules on autonomous weapons
briefs.summary: Diplomats in Geneva agreed at 4:30 a.m. Saturday to give countries two years to propose rules that may be binding or optional. The Red Cross had sought binding rules within a year; the U.S. proposed five years of nonbinding guidelines.

briefs.headline: Planted secrets trace AI prompt leaks through resellers
briefs.summary: Dragos researcher HD Moore seeded nearly 2 million prompts with trackable credentials and found at least three providers compromised; OpenRouter has since told customers prompts sent to China-based MiniMax may have been read.

kicker: Putnam-Kanawha carries no regional line today; buck firearms season opens Monday in 51 counties.
